Description: wdotool-core: the substrate every backend builds on. Backend trait, detector, capabilities reporting, keysym parser, portal token cache, value types, error model. UI-agnostic and intentionally small. Adding a new backend slots in here without touching the CLI; adding a CLI command exercises the same trait.

Five backend implementations: wlr-protocols for Sway/Hyprland/river/Wayfire, libei for the XDG RemoteDesktop portal, kde for KWin scripting on top of libei, gnome for the companion Shell extension on top of libei, and uinput as the compositor-agnostic fallback. Each backend runs on a dedicated OS thread because the underlying event streams aren't Send.

The wdotool binary: input commands (key, type, mousemove, click, scroll), window commands (search, getactivewindow, windowactivate, windowclose, getwindow*, getmouselocation, outputs), diagnostic commands (info, diag), prime mode, and xdotool argv compat. Thin wrapper around wdotool-core; the dispatch path is structured so it can be driven from an in-process test harness.

Capture user input via the XDG RemoteDesktop portal (libei in receiver mode) or /dev/input/event* via evdev, emit a stream of RecEvents, and replay them through the active backend. Same crate that wflow's recorder lifts as a library dependency. Closes the loop from "capture once" to "replay anywhere".

The headless-sway integration harness, the in-process mock backend, the unit suite, and the real-hardware verification matrices for KDE and GNOME. Where we prove backends work on something other than the maintainer's Hyprland box. Issues #1 (KDE) and #4 (GNOME) gate the verified claims in the README.

Get wdotool onto users' machines. crates.io for cargo users, AUR for Arch (three flavors), DEB/RPM via cargo-dist, a Nix flake, a Containerfile for Podman/Docker, Flathub for the desktop install, and the @wdotool/capabilities npm package for JS/TS consumers parsing capabilities JSON.

wdotool as a first-class citizen of Drift OS. Bundled in the ISO, a `drift` backend that goes through Drift's own compositor protocols (same shape kde and gnome already use), first-boot setup that primes the portal consent + uinput group + prime service, a Drift Settings "Automation" panel powered by the capabilities schema, and synthetic-input-provenance hooks the Drift compositor uses to tag injected events with the injecting PID.

wdotool's first known library consumer. The recorder module migration that turned wflow's bundled recorder into a wdotool-core dep, the public API stability we owe wflow as a substrate library, and the capability-descriptor surface wflow's first-run trust prompt consults to tell users what a workflow can do before they accept it.

async_trait Backend on top of dedicated worker threads (the libei/wayland event streams aren't Send). Detector probes XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP, compositor hints (HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE, SWAYSOCK), portal availability, and falls through a preference order with sensible skips when an inner backend fails (e.g. don't retry bare libei after the kde-dbus path already timed on libei).

`wdotool capabilities --json` emits a structured report that downstream consumers parse (wflow, dashboards, Drift Settings). The JSON Schema lives at docs/capabilities-schema.json and is the source of truth for the @wdotool/capabilities npm package. The schema is locked on enum values; adding a capability is a coordinated schema + Rust types + npm types change.

Parse `ctrl+shift+a` into the press-order / release-order sequences xdotool emits. Bare keysyms (Return, Up, F1) and Unicode chars. The compat parity table at docs/xdotool-compat.md tracks what works, what's partial, and what's intentionally out of scope.

libei restore_token persisted at $XDG_STATE_HOME/wdotool/portal.token (mode 0600). First run prompts for consent; later runs present the token and skip the dialog. Token-rejection recovery flow re-runs consent without clobbering a still-valid cache on transient failures.

zwp_virtual_keyboard_v1 + zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1 + zwlr_foreign_toplevel_management_v1 + wl_output. Transient xkb keymap upload at type time (one keycode per unique character as a Level-0 Unicode keysym) is how arbitrary Unicode types end-to-end on this backend without a server-side keymap change. Preferred on Sway, Hyprland, river, Wayfire.

org.freedesktop.portal.RemoteDesktop session, libei socket negotiation, sender-context handshake, input through the compositor's own libei implementation. Full focus awareness and a permission prompt on first run. Preferred on GNOME and KDE.

libei for input + KWin scripting over D-Bus for window management. Generates small JS snippets, hands them to KWin via loadScript / loadScriptFromText, runs them, receives results on a transient com.wdotool.KdeBridge D-Bus service the backend registers at startup. Plasma 5 (workspace.clientList / activeClient) and Plasma 6 (workspace.windowList / activeWindow) supported.

libei (via GNOME's RemoteDesktop portal) + a companion GNOME Shell extension that exposes ListWindows, GetActiveWindow, ActivateWindow, CloseWindow, GetPointerPosition, GetWindowGeometry on the session bus. GNOME Shell has no generic external window API, so the extension is the only path.

Virtual input device via /dev/uinput, raw input_event writes. Compositor-agnostic but no focus awareness and no window API. The fallback for environments without libei or the wlr-* protocols. Usual setup is usermod -aG uinput $USER plus a udev rule.

key / keydown / keyup / type / mousemove / click / mousedown / mouseup / scroll. The bread-and-butter xdotool argv that scripts rely on. --clearmodifiers approximates xdotool's behavior (Wayland has no API to observe current modifier state).

search (with --name, --class, --pid, --regex, --ignore-case, --any), getactivewindow, windowactivate, windowclose, getwindowname / pid / classname, getwindowgeometry, getmouselocation, outputs. Surfaces what each backend can actually do; the wlr-protocols backend stubs out non-supported queries with a clear error rather than guessing.

info (detected backend + capabilities), diag (env + backend availability report, markdown or JSON, --copy pipes through wl-copy/xclip). diag is the first thing to run for a bug report; it probes pre-conditions only and never opens a portal session, so it can't pop a consent dialog by mistake.

`wdotool prime` is a long-running foreground command that creates and holds the wlroots virtual_keyboard + virtual_pointer alive on the compositor's seat until SIGINT or SIGTERM. Prints ready to stdout then blocks. Scripts running many wdotool ops in sequence avoid per-call virtual-device latency; integration test harnesses get a stable seat-cap to bind against.

Global --backend <libei|wlr-protocols|kde|gnome|uinput> bypasses detection. wlroots is still accepted as an alias for wlr-protocols. WDOTOOL_LIBEI_TIMEOUT_SECS tunes the portal device-resume timeout (default 15s, was 5s pre-0.5.1).

libei in receiver mode through the XDG RemoteDesktop portal. Production target for capture on GNOME / KDE / any portal-enabled session. Inherits the same consent + token cache as the sender-mode libei backend.

/dev/input/event* via evdev as the fallback recorder when the portal isn't available. Needs the `input` group on most distros. Wrapped behind the same RecorderConfig::BackendChoice cascade so a caller asks for `auto` and gets portal then evdev with no surprises.

`wdotool replay <file>` reads a trace JSON, plays Gap events for timing fidelity, and dispatches each RecEvent through the active backend. --speed scales the gaps. Same keysym / mouse-button / scroll helpers as the sender CLI, so modifier ordering matches.
`wdotool record` and `wdotool replay`, both gated behind the recorder Cargo feature (default-on for the released binary). --max-duration auto-stops; -o writes a file; `-` reads from stdin on replay.

wdotool-test-harness crate boots sway with WLR_BACKENDS=headless, spawns the wdotool-observer (a small wayland-client + xkbcommon binary that prints received input events), runs wdotool against the same display, and asserts on what events the compositor actually delivered. CI installs sway with WLR_RENDERER=pixman on GitHub runners.

MockBackend in wdotool-core/src/backend/mock.rs behind the `testing` Cargo feature. dispatch() takes a DispatchCtx { backend, env, stdout, stderr } and returns a structured ExitCode rather than calling process::exit, so integration tests drive every CLI subcommand against the mock and assert on the exact BackendCall sequence.

Walk docs/verification/kde-plasma-6.md on real Plasma 6 hardware. 13 operations x 6 conditions matrix. Closes the input side via libei (shipped v0.5.2) and the window-ops side via KWin scripting (shipped v0.5.3). Issue #1 stays open until someone walks the full matrix and posts it back.

Same shape as KDE verification: install the wdotool@wdotool.github.io Shell extension, run the smoke matrix, post the diag report. Blocked locally on the host's nvidia-drm modeset=0 setting; GNOME Wayland needs modeset=1 to get a DRM master. Either flip the host setting and reboot or set up a GNOME VM. Issue #4.

`cargo install wdotool` and `wdotool-core` as a library dep. crates.io is the canonical address for Rust consumers; wflow links wdotool-core from here. Each release tags a coordinated bump across wdotool, wdotool-core, and wdotool-test-harness.

Three flavors: wdotool (source build at the latest stable tag), wdotool-bin (prebuilt x86_64 binary from the GitHub release), wdotool-git (rolling build from main). pkgver derives from the release tag.

App ID io.github.cushycush.wdotool. Manifest at packaging/flatpak/io.github.cushycush.wdotool.yml builds locally. AppStream metainfo + .desktop ready. Submission to flathub/flathub is the remaining manual step.

Podman-native, Docker-compatible Containerfile at packaging/container/. Debian-slim plus runtime deps; binary installed from a release .deb. wlroots and uinput backends work inside the container; libei/kde/gnome don't (portal forwarding is a rabbit hole, Flatpak is the more reliable path for those). Shipped in v0.5.2; closes issue #39.
distros.yml CI workflow runs alongside cargo-dist's release on every tag push, builds .deb and .rpm artifacts, attaches them to the same GitHub Release. Shipped in v0.2.0.
flake.nix lets users run `nix run github:cushycush/wdotool -- --help` or import the input into a NixOS / home-manager config. Shipped.

TypeScript types and the JSON Schema document for `wdotool capabilities` output. Shipped in v0.3.0. CI fails if the locked enums in src/types.ts drift from docs/capabilities-schema.json. First publish was manual via the npm publish workflow; @wdotool org + NPM_TOKEN are configured.

Drift ISO ships with wdotool pre-installed (alongside wflow), the uinput udev rule and group set up, and the portal consent primed at first login. Matches WFLOW-46 / DRIFT-56 (bundling user-owned tools) and the DRIFT CLI epic. No extra install step to get to a working state.

A new `drift` backend slot alongside kde.rs and gnome.rs that goes through Drift's own compositor IPC for window ops (and, eventually, input). Same shape kde + gnome already use: libei (or Drift's portal frontend) for input + a Drift-specific IPC path for window queries. Lets Drift evolve its protocols without forcing the wlr-* compatibility scope.

Drift first-boot wizard adds the user to the uinput group, installs the udev rule for /dev/uinput, runs `wdotool diag --json` to confirm every backend the session supports is green, and optionally enables the wdotool-prime user service. Pairs with DRIFT-45 (first-boot starter workflows) on the wflow side.

Drift Settings GUI gets an Automation tab that parses `wdotool diag --json` and the @wdotool/capabilities schema and shows the user what works on their setup: backends, portal token state, uinput access. Buttons to reset consent, probe backends, run a smoke test, copy a markdown bug report.

Drift compositor wants to tag injected events with the injecting PID so downstream tools can attribute them. wdotool's side: surface a stable client tag on the libei session and (where the wire format allows) include the PID on every emitted event. Closes DRIFT-27.

Summary: prime as a Drift systemd user service
Description: Drift dotfiles ship a wdotool-prime.service user unit that starts on login, runs `wdotool prime`, and keeps the wlroots virtual devices alive on the seat for the session. Every wdotool invocation in the session is instantaneous; user can disable from Drift Settings.

Today wdotool and wflow each open their own org.freedesktop.portal.RemoteDesktop session and each pay one consent prompt. A shared session (mediated by Drift's portal frontend or a small daemon) cuts the prompt count from N to 1 and gets faster startup.
Type "diag" or "test input" in the Drift Launcher and get a one-shot result card from `wdotool diag`. Copy-to-clipboard, run smoke, reset consent. Reuses the existing diag --copy path.

wflow's bundled recorder (~1100 lines in src/recorder.rs) lifted into wdotool-core::recorder as a substrate library behind the `recorder` Cargo feature. wflow swaps over to consume this module. Shipped in v0.4.0; design doc at docs/design/recorder-migration.md.

Public surface: Backend trait, DynBackend, detector::{build, Environment, BackendKind}, keysym::parse_chain, value types (Capabilities, WindowInfo), WdoError / Result. Per-backend types stay private. Each release runs the wflow consumer build to catch source-incompatible changes before they ship.

wflow's first-run trust dialog wants to tell the user what a workflow can actually do ("this uses type, click, and windowclose") before they accept it. wdotool side: expose per-action capability metadata that wflow's KDL decoder maps onto its trust prompt. Pairs with WFLOW-13.

wflow links wdotool-core from crates.io; wflow users also run a system wdotool binary for any CLI invocation. The crate dep and the system binary are independent installs and stay version-compatible per release. Documented in wflow packaging (WFLOW-32).

`mousemove --output <name>` lands on the right output on multi-monitor setups. wlroots backend overrides Backend::mouse_move_to_output to bind a per-output virtual_pointer via create_virtual_pointer_with_output. Shipped in v0.5.0; closes issue #22.

Track currently-depressed XKB modifier bitmask in the worker thread, map named modifier keysyms to xkb mod indices via keymap.mod_get_index(), call vk.modifiers() before each modifier press and after each release. Without this, Hyprland and other wlr compositors didn't auto-derive the seat's modifier state from virtual-keyboard key events, so chords didn't hold. Shipped in v0.4.0.

Every input op does a queue.roundtrip() after sending protocol messages and before returning, so a fast wdotool process can't exit and destroy its virtual devices before the compositor finishes processing in-flight events. Caught by the new Layer 3 round-trip tests. Shipped in v0.5.0.

Summary: Rename wlroots Cargo feature to wlr-protocols
Description: The runtime backend is wlr-protocols (renamed in v0.5.2). The Cargo feature flag is still named wlroots because renaming forces a breaking change on every downstream Cargo.toml at the same time. Coordinated with a wflow update (it's the only known downstream) and a wdotool-core 0.6.0 bump.
$XDG_STATE_HOME/wdotool/portal.token cached at mode 0600, presented on every subsequent run, transparent recovery when the token is rejected. Shipped in v0.2.0.

Binding Keyboard alongside Pointer or PointerAbsolute in one ei_seat.bind call makes KWin silently drop the keyboard device. Filed upstream at bugs.kde.org#520464; worked around client-side by doing a two-stage bind (keyboard alone first, then the full set). Combined with the missing-flush fix, this is what made libei work end-to-end on Plasma 6. Shipped in v0.5.2.

Bumped libei device-resume timeout from 5s to 15s; cold-start of xdg-desktop-portal-kde can take longer than 5s on a fresh boot. Override via WDOTOOL_LIBEI_TIMEOUT_SECS. Error now lists candidate causes instead of asserting the user dismissed the dialog. Shipped in v0.5.1; closes part of issue #40.

When a kde-dbus or gnome-ext init fails because its inner libei timed out, skip the bare-libei retry that comes next in the priority list. Previously the user waited the libei timeout twice in a row before seeing a real error. Shipped in v0.5.1; closes issue #40.

Plasma 6 removed loadScriptFromText. run_kwin_script now writes the generated JS to a tempfile, calls loadScript(filePath, pluginName) with a per-call plugin name, and executes via the per-script /Scripting/Script{id} object's run() method. Two subtle Plasma 6 issues surfaced during live verification: callDBus can't reach well-known D-Bus names (so we route through the session bus unique name), and callDBus serializes JS numbers as int32 (so req_id had to drop from u64). Shipped in v0.5.3; closes issue #45.

wdotool@wdotool.github.io extension exposes ListWindows, GetActiveWindow, ActivateWindow, CloseWindow on org.wdotool.GnomeShellBridge. Targets GNOME Shell 45 through 48. No background activity; responds to D-Bus only. Shipped in v0.1.6.

GetPointerPosition method backs `wdotool getmouselocation` on GNOME. Calls global.get_pointer(). Reinstall the extension if a copy older than v0.4.0 is in ~/.local/share/gnome-shell/extensions/. Shipped in v0.4.0.
GetWindowGeometry method backs `wdotool getwindowgeometry` on GNOME. Calls MetaWindow.get_frame_rect(). Shipped in v0.4.0.

packaging/container/README.md walks running wdotool from inside a Podman/Docker container against a host Wayland session: --device /dev/uinput, --group-add, the udev rule. Closes the gap for CI rigs that don't want to install host packages.

`wdotool type` uploads a transient xkb keymap at type time (one keycode per unique character as a Level-0 Unicode keysym) on the wlroots backend, so arbitrary Unicode works end-to-end without a server-side keymap change. libei / kde / gnome / uinput stay best-effort because the compositor or kernel owns the keymap.

`wdotool outputs` and `wdotool outputs --json` enumerate the compositor's monitors. Each row carries name, origin in compositor coords, logical size, and integer scale. Modern wlroots compositors put real positions on xdg_output.logical_position; backend now binds zxdg_output_manager_v1 and falls back to wl_output.geometry. Shipped in v0.4.0.

`wdotool getmouselocation` prints x:N y:N (xdotool's default format). First read-side input API in wdotool; every prior command was send-side. KDE reads workspace.cursorPos; GNOME calls global.get_pointer(); libei / wlroots / uinput exit 1 (their protocols are send-only by design). Shipped in v0.4.0.

`wdotool getwindowgeometry <id>` prints xdotool's three-line format (window header, position, geometry). KDE via kwin script reading window.frameGeometry; GNOME via the Shell extension. wlroots / libei / uinput exit 1 with a clear stderr message because the underlying protocols don't expose geometry. Shipped in v0.4.0.

`wdotool search` grew real matchers: --class (Wayland app_id), --pid (exact process id), --regex (full regex on --name / --class), --ignore-case, --any (OR instead of AND). Exit code semantics match xdotool: 1 when nothing matches, 0 when at least one window matches. Shipped in v0.3.0.

`wdotool diag --copy` pipes the markdown report through wl-copy (falling back to xclip). Bug-report ergonomics: "run this, paste the output into the issue." --json for machine-readable. Shipped in v0.2.0.

13 operations x 6 conditions on a real Plasma 6 box. Maintainer doesn't run KDE; either wait for a community walkthrough (Twig6943 / hron have been in touch via the wflow Discord) or set up a Plasma 6 VM. Closes issue #1.

Summary: Install extension + walk the GNOME smoke checklist
Description: Install wdotool@wdotool.github.io from packaging/gnome-extension/, run a few wdotool commands, post the diag report. Blocked on issue #71.

Summary: Unblock GNOME on this host (nvidia-drm modeset=1)
Description: GNOME Wayland login freezes on this host because /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf sets nvidia-drm modeset=0 (flipped down from =1 on 2026-05-11; .bak file is the smoking gun). Mutter on NVIDIA needs modeset=1 to get a DRM master. Two paths: flip the option back and regen initramfs, or set up a GNOME VM. Blocks WDOTOOL-70.
Manifest at packaging/flatpak/io.github.cushycush.wdotool.yml builds locally. Submit to flathub/flathub. AppStream metainfo + .desktop are ready.

Summary: Probe Drift compositor's IPC for window ops
Description: Read drift-compositor's IPC surface and decide whether the wlr-protocols backend's foreign-toplevel-management is enough or whether Drift's own protocols give us something better (window-class lookups by pid, frame-aware geometry, etc.). Informs the shape of WDOTOOL-74.

New wdotool-core/src/backend/drift.rs alongside kde.rs and gnome.rs. Composes libei (input) with Drift compositor IPC (window ops). Detector picks it on XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=drift or when the drift-session compositor identity is present.

Summary: Negotiate client-tag protocol with Drift compositor
Description: Agree on a wire-level tag (libei client_name plus a Drift-specific protocol extension, or just the existing libei sender name) that the Drift compositor reads off our session and surfaces on its IPC event stream as source={kind: synthetic, tool: wdotool, pid: N}. Closes the wdotool half of DRIFT-27.

Summary: Expose injecting PID on libei sessions
Description: Set a stable, parseable client name on the libei session (current libei API supports a name hint; verify what KDE/GNOME/Drift portals do with it) so any future provenance work has a reliable handle. Independent of the protocol-extension half.

Drift Settings (QML) imports the JSON Schema from @wdotool/capabilities and parses `wdotool diag --json`. Per-row UI: backend, available, source-of-truth (auto / manual override), one-click "reset consent" / "run smoke" / "copy diag for bug report".
Drift dotfiles ship a systemd user unit (Type=simple, ExecStart=/usr/bin/wdotool prime). Starts on graphical session start, dies on session end. Drift Settings has a toggle for it.

First-boot wizard step opens an org.freedesktop.portal.RemoteDesktop session under a clearly-labeled "Set up automation" prompt. The user accepts the consent dialog in a context they understand rather than mid-workflow when wflow first runs an action. Stores the resulting restore_token via wdotool's portal_token cache so every consumer (wdotool CLI, wflow, ad-hoc scripts) skips the dialog later. Idea 4 from docs/design/drift-integration.md.

Summary: uinput group + udev rule in Drift base install
Description: Drift base install ships with the /dev/uinput udev rule (60-uinput.rules: KERNEL=="uinput", MODE="0660", GROUP="uinput", OPTIONS+="static_node=uinput") and adds the default user to the uinput group at first boot. No usermod -aG uinput step after first install. One less footgun. Idea 5 from docs/design/drift-integration.md; separated from the broader first-boot setup so the install-image team can land it independently.

Summary: Themed consent dialog via Drift portal frontend
Description: When xdg-desktop-portal asks for input-injection consent, the dialog wears Drift's brand instead of the host desktop's default. Drift owns (or wraps) xdg-desktop-portal-*; the dialog frontend is a visible touchpoint signalling "this is part of Drift, not a generic Linux dialog". Lower-priority polish, but a real touchpoint. Idea 8 from docs/design/drift-integration.md.

Summary: Drift IPC events as wdotool-core triggers
Description: wdotool-core grows an events module that exposes Drift compositor IPC events (window-opened, workspace-switched, app-focused, idle-threshold; DRIFT-42) as a Stream<Event> other Rust code subscribes to. Same shape as the recorder module already takes. wflow consumes the stream and turns each event into a trigger card. Drift compositor stays the source of truth; wdotool-core is the consumer-side Rust facade so other tools (wflow, third-party) don't each re-implement the IPC client. Idea 11 from docs/design/drift-integration.md.

New wdotool-core/src/events/ module gated behind an events Cargo feature (mirrors the recorder feature shape). Subscribes to Drift compositor's IPC, decodes events into a typed enum, exposes via a tokio-stream Stream<Event>. Behind an explicit feature flag because Drift IPC is the only event source today; uinput and wlr-protocols don't have one. Pairs with WFLOW-side ticket for the trigger-card consumer.

Lock @wdotool/capabilities as the single source of truth for "what can this session do". Three consumers: Drift Settings (WDOTOOL-77), wflow's first-run trust prompt (WDOTOOL-48), and the Drift docs site's per-backend feature matrix. CI already fails on drift between docs/capabilities-schema.json, the npm package's src/types.ts, and the Rust types in wdotool-core/src/capabilities.rs; extending the same gate to Drift Settings (QML import + a smoke test) and the Drift docs site locks in three-way schema parity. Idea 13 from docs/design/drift-integration.md.
